_methodology: Each claim is a falsifiable prediction. If field data or a model run refutes it, update the claim text and record the refutation -- do NOT retune the simulation to preserve the prediction. The simulation is a measurement instrument, not an argument.

claims.original_claim: The region with the highest channel multiplier (exposure_multiplier()) will rank highest on EWRI, because the channel -- not the source contamination level -- is the primary injury driver.
claims.original_reasoning: Even a moderately contaminated batch becomes a human-injury event when it lands in a region with near-zero QC, high price pressure, and no buffer. Source severity is bounded by scrap carryover ranges; channel multiplier varies more widely and should dominate.
claims.test: Run scan (seed=1, n=20000). Check if argmax(exposure_multiplier) == argmax(EWRI).
claims.refutation: Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest channel multiplier (3.57) but ranks #2 on EWRI (7.43). Cuba ranks #1 (EWRI 8.57) with a lower multiplier (3.36) because its embargo-forced recycled_fraction=0.85 produces substantially more contaminated batches, and its medical/food product reliance weights are among the highest. Neither term universally dominates.
claims.updated_claim: EWRI is a compound of source severity (driven by recycled_fraction and product reliance) and channel (multiplier). A very high recycled fraction with extreme product reliance can outrank a higher-channel region with lower scrap content. Both terms must be assessed -- no single variable is sufficient.

claims.claim: Pb is the dominant injury vector for food_can and medical product classes in every modelled region, regardless of region ranking.
claims.reasoning: Pb threshold for food_can (0.010 wt%) and medical (0.005 wt%) is the lowest of any contaminant. Scrap carryover spans 0.001--0.30 wt% with a heavy upper tail. Even at the median, Pb exceedance probability is high enough to dominate the vector count.
claims.test: Run scan; inspect dominant_vector[food_can] and dominant_vector[medical] for all regions.
claims.note: CONFIRMED in model. Field confirmation requires XRF batch sampling. Model confirmation alone does not validate the carryover distribution -- it only shows internal consistency with the scrap_carryover ranges in contaminants.py. Replace ranges with measured values as they arrive.
claims.falsification_condition: Any region where Fe, Si, or Mn records a higher vector_count than Pb for food_can or medical over >= 10,000 batches.

claims.claim: Mn is the dominant injury vector for the electrical product class in every modelled region.
claims.reasoning: Mn has the highest conductivity_penalty_per_0p1 (0.34% IACS per 0.1 wt%) and the lowest injury threshold for electrical (0.05 wt%). The scrap carryover range (0.05--0.80 wt%) means most batches exceed threshold.
claims.test: Run scan; inspect dominant_vector[electrical] for all regions.
claims.note: CONFIRMED in model. Mn threshold of 0.05 wt% for conductor-grade Al is tight; real 1xxx-series wire allows up to ~0.05 wt% Mn by spec (AA1350). If field data shows higher tolerance in practice, raise the threshold and re-run.
claims.falsification_condition: Any region where Fe or Si records a higher vector_count than Mn for electrical over >= 10,000 batches.

claims.claim: The p95/mean EWRI ratio exceeds 1.30 for US inner-city and US rural poor regions, reflecting a heavier bad-batch tail than top-ranked regions.
claims.reasoning: Cuba and Sub-Saharan Africa have high baseline recycled_fraction, so even median batches are severely contaminated -- the tail is not much worse than the mean. US regions have lower recycled_fraction; most batches are mild, but a contaminated-scrap spike (Pb/Cd) lands on people with no QC or buffer. The tail event is disproportionately bad relative to the mean.
claims.test: Run scan (seed=1, n=20000). Compute ewri_p95 / ewri for us_inner_city and us_rural_poor. Assert > 1.30.
claims.note: Currently sits at 1.32, just above the 1.30 threshold. Sensitive to seed and n_batches. Retest at n=100000 across 10 seeds before treating as confirmed.
claims.falsification_condition: Ratio < 1.30 for either US region at n=100000 averaged across seeds 1-10.

claims.claim: Structural class shows no dominant injury vector (recorded as '-') in any region with recycled_fraction <= 0.60, because structural thresholds are high enough that median scrap batches do not breach them.
claims.reasoning: Structural thresholds: Fe 0.70, Si 0.80, Cu 0.40, Mn 1.50, Zn 1.00 wt%. These are above the midpoint of most scrap_carryover ranges. Only high-recycled-fraction supply (rec >= ~0.75) generates enough batches above threshold to accumulate a dominant vector.
claims.test: Inspect dominant_vector[structural] for all regions. Assert '-' for any region with recycled_fraction <= 0.60.
claims.note: Holds in current model. Cuba (rec=0.85) does record Si as structural dominant. Boundary is between rec=0.60 (India, '-') and rec=0.85 (Cuba, 'Si'). Claim should be retested if any region is updated to rec >= 0.70.
claims.falsification_condition: Any region with recycled_fraction <= 0.60 records a non-'-' structural dominant vector.

claims.claim: Raising Cuba's qc_capacity from 0.20 to 0.40 (plausible with a donated XRF program) reduces its EWRI by more than 15% without changing any other parameter.
claims.reasoning: qc_capacity enters the channel multiplier as (0.5 + (1 - qc)). Cuba at qc=0.20 contributes factor 1.30; at qc=0.40 it contributes 1.10. Multiplier scales all batch EWRI samples. The reduction should propagate linearly through the mean.
claims.test: Run scan with Cuba qc_capacity overridden to 0.40 via --local overlay. Compare EWRI to baseline.
claims.falsification_condition: EWRI reduction < 15% -- would imply the multiplier contribution of qc is smaller than modelled, possibly because another channel variable (price_pressure=0.95, buffer=0.08) is the binding constraint.
